items.title: Bajaj Pulsar 220 To Get New Gen – No Upgrades For P180, F250
items.summary: As confirmed by Bajaj Auto, Pulsar 220 is set to get a major new gen upgrade, while the Classic Pulsar 180 and Pulsar F250 won't get updates
items.text: Saying Indian enthusiasts are fond of Bajaj Pulsar 220, is an understatement. Even though the company discontinued it in favour of Pulsar F250, the demand for Pulsar 220 was such that Bajaj had to re-launch it. Pulsar 220 continues to be on sale to date, but is yet to receive a new gen treatment, similar to New Gen Classic Pulsar 150 and Pulsar 125. At a recent media QnA in Pune city, Bajaj confirmed that Pulsar 220 will get a new gen upgrade. These upgrades are expected to be similar in ethos as the New Gen Classic Pulsar 150 and Pulsar 125. While the company did not mention an exact timeline, New Gen Classic Pulsar 220 is expected to launch in early 2027, after the launch of their upcoming ADV . Bajaj Auto’s Classic Pulsar lineup consists of four models across four displacement categories. Range starts with Pulsar 125, followed by Pulsar 150, Pulsar 180 and the iconic Pulsar 220. First launched in July 2007, Pulsar 220 has basically remained the same, except for a few minor tweaks here and there. As confirmed by Bajaj, a major upgrade in terms of a new gen treatment is underway for Pulsar 220. When launched, it will be the most significant update to this motorcycle, ever. These updates are expected to be in line with what the recent Classic Pulsars got. items.title: Motorcycle Exports H1 FY2027 – Boxer, Star City, Pulsar, CT, FZ, Apache, Gixxer, Raider, Xtreme
items.summary: India’s motorcycle exports grew 31.83% during April–September 2026, with Boxer and Star City together contributing nearly 46% of overseas shipments.
items.text: India’s motorcycle exports reached 27,64,662 units in the first half of FY2027, up 31.83% from 20,97,158 units in April–September 2025. Overseas shipments increased by 6,67,504 units, driven primarily by substantial gains for Bajaj Boxer and TVS Star City. Total two-wheeler exports stood at 32,07,357 units in H1 FY2027, growing 31.86% over 24,32,412 units. Motorcycles contributed 86.20% of shipments. Scooter exports expanded faster at 34.95% to 4,35,363 units, accounting for 13.57% of the total. Moped exports declined 42.03% to 7,332 units, contributing the remaining 0.23%. Bajaj Boxer retained the top position with 6,68,804 units, growing 90.56% over 3,50,972 units a year earlier. Its increase of 3,17,832 units was the largest among the ranked motorcycle families, taking its share of motorcycle exports to 24.19%. TVS Star City followed with 6,01,720 units, up 46.06% from 4,11,961 units. It added 1,89,759 units and accounted for 21.76% of shipments. Together, Boxer and Star City contributed 45.95% of motorcycle exports . Their combined increase of 5,07,591 units represented approximately 76% of the segment’s net export growth. Bajaj Pulsar ranked third with 3,01,449 units, up 17.26%, while CT followed with 2,15,040 units, growing 31.89%. The top four entries collectively accounted for 64.63% of motorcycle exports. items.text: The recently launched Bonneville T40 was the first of the Bajaj-built Triumph models to feature a circular colour TFT display with riding modes and cruise control. It now looks like these features might trickle down to the other models, as a Thruxton 400 has been spotted testing with the TFT dash. The suite of rider aids on the current Thruxton 400 is limited to a simple traction control system, which can be switched off, as well as non-switchable dual-channel ABS. This particular test mule with the TFT dash could augment that with additions like riding modes and cruise control (seen via the switchgear on the LH switch cube). It’s worth noting that this seems like a test mule of the export-spec Thruxton 400 because it is wearing Pirelli Rosso 4 rubber (the tyres supplied on the bike in international markets). As such, it remains to be seen if the India-spec Thruxton 400 will also be updated with these features. So far, aside from the different engines owing to GST, the export-spec and India-spec Triumph 400s have been in sync when it comes to features, and only time will tell if that continues to be the case going forward. items.text: Just a couple of days after the global unveiling of the updated Tiger 1200 range , Triumph has revealed pricing for the two variants – the GT Pro and Rally Explorer – that will be available in India from March 2027. The updated flagship adventure models receive substantial updates, including a more powerful engine, a revised chassis setup and radar-based rider aids. The updated 1,160cc liquid-cooled triple now makes 158hp at 9,250rpm (8hp more than before) and 130Nm at 6,750rpm, with peak torque arriving lower in the rev range. Triumph has redesigned the cylinder head, pistons and exhaust, and fitted lighter intake and exhaust valves and more precise fuel injection. Along with the increased low-speed torque and revised primary and final-drive ratios, the crawl speed is lower by 6kph. Both variants now use a 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheel combination, meaning the Tiger 1200 will no longer be available with a 21-inch front wheel, as in previous generations. The GT Pro has cast aluminium wheels, while the Rally Explorer has spoked wheels. The suspension setup comprises semi-active Showa units, with a 49mm USD fork and a monoshock, both offering 200mm of travel. The system features automatic self-levelling preload and uses inputs from multiple sensors, including a six-axis IMU, to continuously adjust compression and rebound damping. items.title: SMK Ares at Rs 6,950 Brings Serious Dual-Sport Value

items.text: SMK Ares has been launched in India at a starting price of Rs 6,950 inclusive of taxes as the new dual-sport full-face helmet. All three are offered in six colour options giving you 18 combinations across gloss and matte finishes to puck from. Sizes range from XS to XXL and sales have begun through SMK’s authorised dealer network. Online availability will follow later. Ares has been designed around mixed use, combining a detachable sun peak for trail riding with a conventional main visor for road use and an integrated internal sun visor for changing light conditions. This gives you the option of using the same helmet for weekday commuting, highway touring and trail riding. The peak can be removed when not required, while the conventional full-face visor keeps the helmet practical for faster road use. items.title: Ducati Monster V2 Dark unveiled, India launch in 2027
items.summary: The Monster V2 Dark minimises theatricality while stripping the Monster down to its dark essentials, with no mechanical changes.
items.text: Ducati has launched the Monster V2 Dark in global markets, priced at EUR 10,990 (or Rs. 11.69 lakh). The Monster was launched in August 2026, the next chapter in the Monster model's storied history. The Monster V2 Dark will serve as the entry-level model, losing out on a few key features while also offering a minimalist, yet sinister blacked-out design. The Monster was Ducati's first street naked motorcycle, launched in 1992. Since then, the Monster has gone through multiple iterations while retaining its core ethos of simplicity and accessibility. The Monster V2 Dark takes a step further, offering the Monster V2 in a proverbially stripped-down variant, finished in Ducati Dark livery. The aesthetic differences go beyond skin-deep, too. Underneath the jet-black bodywork, Ducati has left the frame, exhaust endcaps, and intake snorkel unpainted, contrasting against the black paintwork. The rims are now all-black, losing out on the red highlights found on the standard model. The seat has been changed slightly too, with a uniform choice of material throughout the seat; the Monster Dark also loses out on the rear seat cowl that buyers would normally get as standard equipment. Interestingly, the Monster Dark also loses out on the LED sequential turn indicators from the standard bike, while the Ducati Quick Shift (DQS) bi-directional quickshifter has become an optional accessory. items.text: Yamaha Motor Europe has gradually added retro-themed paint schemes to its model line-up, including a new Legend Blue scheme for the XSR 900 GP heritage streetfighter. The Japanese automaker has now given its middleweight adventure motorcycle, the Ténéré 700 World Rally, a new Heritage White colour for MY2027 that harks back to historic Yamaha machinery of yesteryear. Yamaha's iconic 'speedblock' pattern originated on their racebikes in the 60s and 70s. Yamaha used two major types of speedblock decals, red on white and black on yellow. Both were iconic in their own right and represented Yamaha Racing in different regions. The red-on-white Speedblock was designed by Molly Sanders, tasked with creating a design that would be easily distinguishable on early televisions, even at racing speed. His design spawned the iconic speedblock pattern we know today. The Ténéré series has earned a significant place in Yamaha's history books. Yamaha gifted the Ténéré moniker to the XT600Z model to celebrate winning the infamous Paris-Dakar cross-country rally. No surprises then, that the XT600Z Ténéré also wore the speedblock pattern at some point during its production run. And now the speedblock returns on the 2027 Tenere 700 World Rally. The World Rally variant sits in the middle of the range in Europe, below the World Raid. items.title: Harley-Davidson X350 T Spied Undisguised With Downsized Engine
items.summary: The Harley-Davidson X350 T will be powered by a 349cc, air/oil-cooled engine, which will be a downsized version of the 440cc motor from the X440 T.
items.text: - Likely to be powered by a downsized 349cc version of the 440cc motor - Will benefit from the lower 18 per cent GST rates The Harley-Davidson X350 T has been spied undisguised at a dealership, hinting at its impending launch. The X350 T is expected to share the platform, chassis, cycle parts and styling with the Harley-Davidson X440 T . However, it will get a smaller 349cc engine to benefit from the lower GST rates. It is important to note that the India-spec X350 T is different from the China-spec X350. The latter uses a Benelli-sourced parallel-twin engine, whereas the X350 T is expected to use a downsized version of the single-cylinder engine from the X440 T. While the X440 T uses a 440cc, single-cylinder motor, the Harley-Davidson X350 T is expected to be powered by a 349cc motor. This will allow Harley-Davidson to position it in the sub-350cc category, which attracts 18 per cent GST compared to the 40 per cent applicable on the X 440T. Similar to what Bajaj, Triumph and KTM have done with their respective 400cc engine platforms, we expect Harley-Davidson to follow a similar route by reducing the stroke length while retaining the bore. This approach will help reduce the engine capacity without significantly altering the engine architecture. A quick back-of-the-envelope calculation suggests the downsized 349cc motor could produce approximately 21-22bhp and 30-32Nm of peak torque. These are expected figures, and the final output will only be known once Harley-Davidson…

items.title: SHAD Unveils Terra Crash Bars for BMW R 1300 GS
items.summary: SHAD is expanding its Terra adventure range into motorcycle protection with upper and lower crash bars for the BMW R 1300 GS. Possible India availability after EICMA 2026.
items.text: SHAD Terra crash bars for the BMW R 1300 GS are set to make their show debut at EICMA 2026. This is an important expansion of the Spanish accessory maker’s adventure-focused Terra range. Until now Terra has largely been associated with panniers, top boxes and soft luggage. The addition of motorcycle protection takes the range into a new category and SHAD has chosen one of the most established large adventure motorcycles as its first application. There’s two separate protection systems for the BMW R 1300 GS. Upper Crash Bars are designed to protect the fuel tank, radiator and upper bodywork. The Lower Crash Bars concentrate on the engine, crankcase or oil sump area and exhaust headers. This modular arrangement is useful because owners can choose the degree of protection they need. Although the upper bars require the corresponding lower crash bars to be installed first. Both assemblies are made from AISI 304 stainless steel. SHAD uses 25mm-diameter tubing with a 2mm wall thickness, with the structure designed to provide high strength without adding unnecessary width around the motorcycle. The bars mount directly to the R 1300 GS ’ existing chassis mounting points, meaning installation does not require cutting or drilling the motorcycle. You can pick between two finishes. The silver version uses a sandblasted and electropolished finish intended to improve corrosion resistance and the black version receives a heat-cured powder coating designed to resist abrasion and stone…

items.title: Triumph Thruxton 400 Spied with TFT Display and New Features
items.summary: The new Triumph Thruxton 400 will get features such as riding modes, cruise control, cornering ABS, and cornering traction control.
items.text: The 2026 Triumph Thruxton 400 has been spied with a new circular colour TFT instrument cluster, similar to the unit on the Bonneville T40. The update is expected to bring additional features, including full map mirroring, Bluetooth connectivity, and IMU-based rider aids to the café racer. The new TFT display comes with updated switchgear, including dedicated cruise control buttons. This suggests the new Thruxton 400 will get cruise control, along with cornering ABS, multiple riding modes, and cornering traction control. However, these features are yet to be officially confirmed. Mechanically, the Thruxton 400 is expected to remain unchanged. It will continue to use the 349cc, liquid-cooled engine producing 39.5bhp and 32Nm. The engine is paired with a six-speed gearbox. Similar to the Bonneville T40, Triumph could also offer the Thruxton 400 in a lower-spec variant. This version is likely to get an LCD instrument cluster and conventional rider aids such as dual-channel ABS and traction control, without the IMU-based lean-sensitive electronics expected on the higher-spec model. With the introduction of the Bonneville T40, it was obvious that Triumph would introduce the new features across its entire 400cc range. items.title: Indian Motorcycle Restructures for Growth
items.summary: Indian Motorcycle is adding manufacturing capability and rebuilding its corporate structure after separating from Polaris.
items.text: Indian Motorcycle announces restructuring as it moves away from its former Polaris ownership and establishes itself as an independent motorcycle company. These new changes will now strengthen manufacturing at Spirit Lake in Iowa, create dedicated corporate functions and remove overlapping positions inherited from the previous structure. The restructuring follows Carolwood LP taking official ownership of Indian Motorcycle in February 2026. Indian is now being separated from the shared corporate systems it previously relied on while under Polaris requiring the motorcycle company to establish its own finance, administration and operational teams. Indian Motorcycle has recently added engine production to the plant while also expanding its paint operations. It will help recruit up to 60 additional manufacturing employees as these capabilities grow. The company has spent the past seven months identifying duplicated functions and structural inefficiencies created during the separation from Polaris. Around 70 positions across different parts of the organisation are being eliminated as a result. Indian Motorcycle has had a presence in India for years, but is still a very niche premium brand. The company has six authorised dealerships located in Delhi, Chandigarh, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai and Kochi. items.title: Moto Guzzi Trip 500 unveiled in Europe
items.summary: The Trip 500 is Moto Guzzi's smallest-capacity offering and would be a great option for Indian buyers if launched here.
items.text: Moto Guzzi, part of the Piaggio Group, has unveiled its new Trip 500 roadster in Europe. The Trip 500 will become Moto Guzzi's small-capacity offering when it goes on sale in early 2027, with Moto Guzzi looking to tap into the entry-level roadster market. The Trip 500 comes with a 500cc, liquid-cooled parallel-twin engine, making a claimed 48bhp. With Moto Guzzi falling under the Piaggio Group, it's possible that '500cc' might be a marketing term, and the engine is closely related to Aprilia's 457cc liquid-cooled parallel-twin, evidenced by similar engine cases and the underbelly exhaust. The Trip 500 could come with a different state of tune or gearing to suit the roadster's character. The Trip 500 also uses a USD fork setup and a large front disc with radially-mounted ByBre braking hardware. The Mandello del Lario-based automaker calls the Trip 500 the 'first of a new generation' for Moto Guzzi, bucking the Italian manufacturer's trend of using transversely mounted, air-cooled V-twin engines. The Trip 500's performance targets the A2 license class in Europe, which has a performance cap of 48bhp, and a power-to-weight limit for larger-capacity models. Moto Guzzi hopes the Trip 500 will appeal to newer riders or those returning to motorcycling, and draw them to the Moto Guzzi brand. items.title: Flying Flea C6 Expands to Pune With 10 Centres
items.summary: Royal Enfield’s electric brand has entered its third Indian city with a wide sales and service footprint.
items.text: Flying Flea C6 has expanded to Pune at a price of Rs 2.79 lakh ex-showroom making the city the third Indian market for Royal Enfield’s electric motorcycle brand after Bengaluru and Hyderabad. And at what scale, Flying Flea opened 10 sales and service centres across Pune from the outset. The network covers Pimple Saudagar, Wakad, Market Yard, Wakdewadi, Chinchwad, Kondhwa, Yerawada, Wagholi, Baner and Kasarwadi areas. Dealers include Nomadic Motorbikes, Kings Royal Riders, Dhone Automobiles, Brahma Motors, Hridaan Motors, Legacy Automotive, Chopada Motors and Vogue Motocorp LLP. The expansion follows the C6’s rollout in Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Flying Flea currently operates 12 sales and service centres in Bengaluru and another four in Hyderabad. With Pune adding 10 more, the company now has 26 touchpoints across its first three Indian cities. Royal Enfield says each Pune dealer is equipped to provide both routine maintenance and dedicated technical support. Pune city has a sizeable two-wheeler population, a strong technology and automotive industry presence and a large base of riders already familiar with premium motorcycles. It also has a mix of dense urban commuting and peripheral roads that fits Flying Flea’s city-focused positioning.

items.title: Updated KTM 200 Duke Launched in India at Rs. 2.07 Lakh
items.summary: The updated KTM 200 Duke has been launched in India at Rs. 2.07 lakh (ex-showroom). The motorcycle has received some new features, including a traction control system, a bi-directional quick shifter, among others. Here’s a detailed breakdown:
items.text: KTM has updated the 200 Duke in India, and the bike has received some substantial updates. The updated bike is now priced at Rs. 2.07 lakh (ex-showroom); this makes it Rs. 1,552 more expensive. It now comes with a new ride-by-wire throttle, unlocking some new features alongside tweaks to its underpinnings. On the features front, the bike now gets two riding modes: Street and Rain, likely to alter the throttle response. In addition, the brand has added a traction control system for better safety. An interesting bit taken from the higher-capacity 390 Duke is the crawl feature. This is a low-speed assist that prevents the bike from stalling at lower speeds, and should make city rides a lot easier. Lastly, for spirited riding, the Duke now gets a bidirectional quickshifter for clutchless up- and downshifts. The underpinnings have been revised, with the bike now getting a 43mm inverted fork and a fatter 150-section rear tyre. This is a welcome change, as the brand had updated the bike earlier with a smaller 37mm WP Apex fork and a thinner 140-section tyre, which felt like a slight downgrade . Apart from the features and underpinning changes, the bike now comes with two additional colours: Liquid-carbon and a full black shade. Aside from these, the bike remains mechanically unchanged. It continues to be powered by the same 199.5cc, single-cylinder, liquid-cooled motor producing 24.67bhp and 19.3Nm.

items.title: 2027 Kawasaki Z900 at Rs 9.99 Lakh Barely Changes
items.summary: 2027 Z900 gets two fresh colour schemes and a slightly revised India-spec power figure. Everything else from the electronics, chassis, suspension and braking remain the same.
items.text: Kawasaki India has updated the Z900 for 2027 model year at Rs 9.99 lakh ex-showroom. Now unlike the substantial overhaul that arrived with the previous update, this new MY27 motorcycle is largely a colour and homologation refresh. 2027 Z900 is now available in Ebony with Metallic Carbon Gray and Metallic Spark Black, and the awesome Pearl Blizzard White with Plasma Lime Green. Both these colourways are new to the India-spec motorcycle. The outgoing 2026 Z900 was offered in Metallic Matte Graphenesteel Gray with Metallic Flat Spark Black and Candy Lime Green with Metallic Carbon Gray. Both of which have now disappeared from Kawasaki India’s 2027 listing. There is, however, one small difference in the India-spec engine figures. The new Z900 continues with the 948cc liquid-cooled inline-four, but Kawasaki India now lists maximum output at 121bhp. For comparison, the official 2026 India page listed the same engine at 122bhp with identical torque output. That means the figure has fallen by 1bhp for MY27. Kawasaki has not explained the reason for this change. It could be related to homologation or the way the output is being declared for the latest model year. There is another small numerical difference. Kawasaki India now lists the 2027 Z900 at 213kg kerb, one kilogram heavier than the 212kg figure for the 2026 model. items.text: Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari has proposed allowing motorists to exceed prescribed speed limits by up to 20 percent before being issued speeding challans on expressways. The suggestion could effectively raise the enforcement threshold to 144 km/hr on stretches where the maximum permitted speed is 120 km/hr. Speaking at the Confederation of Indian Industry’s (CII) National Conference on Highways of India’s Future, Gadkari said he had instructed officials not to issue notices to motorists travelling at speeds of up to 120 km/hr. He added that a 20 percent margin could be considered beyond the prescribed limit, with challans issued for violations exceeding that threshold. If implemented on expressways with a 120 km/hr speed limit, the proposed margin would translate into an enforcement threshold of 144 km/hr. However, the proposal does not amount to an increase in the legal speed limit. Motorists are still required to adhere to the posted speed restrictions, and any change in enforcement policy would need to be formally communicated by the authorities. Total expenses for Q2 FY27 expanded by 71 percent year-on-year to Rs 157.14 crore compared with Rs 91.69 crore in the prior-year period. Cost of materials consumed rose to Rs 134.52 crore against Rs 70.51 crore in Q2 FY26. Profit before tax for the quarter reached Rs 16.73 crore against Rs 3.93 crore in Q2 FY26. Total tax expense for the second quarter stood at Rs 5.03 crore, comprising current tax of Rs 5.46 crore and a deferred tax credit of Rs 42.12 lakh. For H1 FY27, Omax Autos recorded a net profit of Rs 22.30 crore, nearly tripling from the Rs 7.48 crore in H1 FY26. Standalone operational revenue for H1 FY27 rose 53 percent to Rs 286.93 crore from Rs 187.92 crore in the prior-year period. Total expenses for the six-month period scaled to Rs 273.40 crore compared to Rs 191.64 crore in H1 FY26.

Here's all you need to know: Powering the Moto Guzzi Trip 500 will be the same 457cc liquid-cooled parallel-twin engine as the Aprilia RS 457 and the Tuono 457 . On the Aprilias, this engine makes 47.6 PS and 43.5 Nm, paired to a 6-speed gearbox with a bidirectional quickshifter. We have experienced this engine on the Aprilia twins, it has a torquey nature and offers effortless pull throughout its rev band. Being a 270-degree crank engine, it also sounds similar to a sporty V-twin, which would suit the Trip 500's character. The Trip 500 stays true to authentic Moto Guzzi styling but with a neo-retro twist. The most noticeable styling element is the round LED headlight with Moto Guzzi wing-inspired LED DRLs, which give it a unique character. The bike also gets a golden-coloured inverted fork, a muscular fuel tank, a single-piece seat and split grab rails that give it a sporty look. The Moto Guzzi bike will be available in four colours: Black Metropolis, Green Grove, Red Bat and ‘The Opening’ special-edition colour scheme. While the Trip 500 shares its frame with the Aprilia twins, its subframe has been modified to accommodate the new side-mounted monoshock. items.text: Updated KTM 200 Duke reaches dealerships Gets a new paint scheme, updated features and more The upcoming KTM 200 Duke has started reaching dealerships ahead of the official launch. The latest update brings a significant equipment upgrade to the popular streetfighter, making it more feature-packed than before. The latest update is considerably more significant, particularly for enthusiasts. The 2026 KTM 200 Duke now gets a bi-directional quickshifter, allowing riders to shift gears without using the clutch, both while upshifting and downshifting. It also gets an electronic throttle (ride-by-wire), which has enabled KTM to introduce two riding modes: Rain and Street. Another notable addition is switchable traction control, with its tell-tale light now visible on the instrument cluster. KTM has also updated the right-side switchgear, replacing the older unit with a newer setup similar to the one seen on the larger 390 Duke. The left-side switchgear, however, remains unchanged. Interestingly, the updated motorcycle spotted at dealerships features a new-looking Black colour scheme. It appears stealthier than the existing Dark Galvano shade, with fewer orange elements across the bodywork. With the addition of a quickshifter, ride-by-wire, riding modes and traction control, the updated KTM 200 Duke gets a substantial equipment boost. The Royal Enfield That Makes Exploring Remote Mountains Easier Than Ever
items.summary: While Royal Enfield is usually known for its easy-going roadsters, this machine has hardcore written all over it to tackle tricky terrain
items.text: Royal Enfield has always had its own meaning of adventure. Most brands seem to think a proper adventure bike needs a giant engine, a ton of horsepower, and more riding modes than anyone will ever actually use, plus a price tag to match. Meanwhile, Royal Enfield’s single-cylinder bikes have been slogging up the high passes of Ladakh for generations, usually overloaded, often underpowered, and somehow still making it to the top, one stubborn thump at a time. All that mountain mileage has produced one bike that turns “too far” into “why not.” Ask most riders to picture a Royal Enfield, and you’ll probably hear the same scene: a thumping single loaded with jerrycans and duffel bags, prayer flags flapping on a dusty pass high in the Himalayas. For decades, that bike was usually a Bullet , a road machine doing a mountain bike’s job, and riders made it work with spare cables, patience, and plenty of pushing. Royal Enfield took the hint and built the Himalayan 411 , its first purpose-built adventure bike, with a 21-inch front wheel and an air-cooled single making around 24 horsepower. After launching in India in 2016, it reached US dealers in April 2018. But it, too, had its limits. At altitude, it ran out of breath, and on the highway it needed the throttle pinned just to keep pace. That red flag sent Royal Enfield back to the drawing board, and what came out was a far more complete take on the formula . That more complete take is the Himalayan 450 . items.summary: Bajaj Auto plans to expand Chetak production amid strong demand.
items.text: Joint Managing Director Rakesh Sharma said production had returned to the existing full capacity after a supply chain disruption affected output. The issue had reduced recent production to around 40,000 units, resulting in a shortfall of 20,000 vehicles despite strong demand. The company expects to remove production bottlenecks during the January-March quarter and bring monthly capacity closer to current requirements. Chetak volumes more than doubled during the July-September quarter, while revenue from the segment crossed Rs. 20 bn. Sharma said electric vehicles (EVs) had become margin accretive for Bajaj Auto rather than reducing margins. Chetak had moved from losses to double-digit profitability, while the company’s three-wheeler business continued to report double-digit profitability and had improved its performance. Bajaj Auto is also evaluating several locations for a new manufacturing facility that would support EV and internal combustion engine (ICE) production. The company is discussing potential sites with a few state governments as it considers its sixth plant, with capacity also being assessed for premium products and high-end motorcycles. The automaker has previously indicated that it aims to increase annual manufacturing capacity by more than 25 per cent in the medium term. events.text: Q1. What’s fuelling India’s fast-growing biking culture right now? A few forces are converging at once. Rising disposable incomes and easier access to finance have put mid-capacity and premium motorcycles within reach of a much younger buyer than we saw a decade ago. At the same time, riding has shifted from being purely a commute or a college obsession to a lifestyle statement — weekend rides, long-distance touring, and motorsport fandom are now aspirational in a way they weren’t before. Almost every city has multiple riding clubs who happen to find a reason to meet over the weekend. Infrastructure has helped too — better highways and mountain roads have opened up touring circuits that simply weren’t practical earlier. accessories.summary: The cruiser will be the third motorcycle born from the Hero-Harley joint venture.
accessories.text: Earlier this month, Harley-Davidson teased the Sprint 440, the third motorcycle from its joint venture (JV) with Hero MotoCorp. Now, the cruiser motorcycle has been spotted at a showroom before its launch. Considering it looks production-ready, we expect the launch to be really close. While all three bikes manufactured under the JV are based on the same platform, the major distinguishing feature of the Sprint 440 is its faithful adherence to the cruiser philosophy compared with the X440 and X440 T . As we reported after the teaser, the motorcycle’s front wheel is markedly larger than the rear one. Considering the X440 bikes already run on an 18/17-inch front/rear tyre setup, the Sprint will likely have either a bigger front tyre or a smaller rear tyre. The fuel tank’s shape is also far more rounded and classical, similar to that of the much bigger Low Rider S and Street Bob . The tank flows into a single-piece, scooped-out bucket seat, with space for a rider and pillion. The seat height also appears markedly lower than that of the X440s, which should make the Sprint accessible to a wider number of buyers. Even the subframe appears to be redesigned, likely to account for the lower seat. The riding position, too, is typical for a cruiser, with an upswept handlebar and ever-so-slightly forward-set foot pegs. KTM 200 Duke Teased with New Electronic Features
accessories.summary: The KTM 200 Duke is expected to cost around Rs 2.09 lakh (ex-showroom), with the latest version adding electronic rider aids and a new-looking black finish.
accessories.text: The KTM 200 Duke is expected to cost around Rs 2.09 lakh (ex-showroom), with the latest version adding electronic rider aids and a new-looking black finish. KTM is preparing another update for the 200 Duke in India, with the revised motorcycle already spotted at dealerships before its official launch. The changes focus on technology and rider assistance, bringing equipment previously associated with larger Duke models to the 200cc streetfighter. The company has yet to confirm the final specifications and pricing. The biggest addition is a bi-directional quickshifter, which allows riders to shift up and down through the gears without operating the clutch. The motorcycle also gets a ride-by-wire throttle, replacing the conventional mechanical throttle connection with an electronic system. This enables two riding modes: Rain and Street. The updated model is also expected to feature traction control, with a corresponding indicator visible on the 5-inch TFT instrument cluster. However, cruise control is not included. KTM has revised the right-side switchgear, giving it a design similar to the unit used on the 390 Duke. The left-side switchgear appears unchanged. The updated motorcycle is expected to retain its 199.5cc, single-cylinder, liquid-cooled petrol engine. It produces 25bhp and 19.3Nm of torque, with a six-speed gearbox transmitting power to the rear wheel. accessories.summary: Honda is considering motocross and enduro bikes for India, where incredible terrain and a growing off-road scene await.
accessories.text: India is one of those places that should be on every adventure rider's bucket list. We're talking towering mountains, rocky trails, muddy forests, and enough challenging terrain to keep even the most experienced dirt bike enthusiasts thoroughly entertained. And while the country has no shortage of motorcycles, there's still plenty of room for more machines designed to tackle the rough stuff. Apparently, Honda has been paying attention. Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India is considering expanding its off-road lineup with dedicated motocross and enduro bikes. Company president and CEO Tsutsumu Otani confirmed that the brand is evaluating both categories, potentially opening the door to some seriously interesting machinery. Nothing's confirmed just yet, but it's a promising development for a market with enormous off-road potential. Honda already sells the XR300L and XR300 Rally in India, giving riders a couple of legitimate options for getting dirty. But its global off-road portfolio goes much further, from the beginner-friendly CRF50F to the competition-ready CRF450R. accessories.text: Classic Legends has taken a big step toward making motorcycle ownership completely hassle-free. They are setting up an authorized distribution network across India to supply genuine spare parts beyond their standard dealership network. This move directly addresses one of the primary expectations of motorcycle owners—getting timely and reliable access to original parts. By expanding availability to independent workshops, local service partners, and customers across urban, semi-urban, and emerging markets, the company aims to speed up part procurement, enhance spare parts availability, and drastically reduce service turnaround times nationwide. Commenting on the launch of the distribution network, Mr. Anupam Thareja, Co-founder of Classic Legends , stated: “As more riders choose Jawa, Yezdi and BSA, delivering a seamless ownership experience remains a key priority for us.
